question: Is Book A (the only strategy that survived the project's tests) a real trend-following edge, or an artefact of its hindsight-selected 5-coin universe (SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, ETH)?
rules: frozen BOOK_A_ALT_RM + BOOK_A_RISK_DEFAULT unchanged: BTC > SMA200 gate, top 6 by 20-day momentum (> 0), inverse-vol weights, 30% vol target, weekly Monday rebalance, $15 minimum position, $250 capital, risk overlay
only_change: universe = ETHUSDT + the point-in-time top-20 alt list of the current calendar quarter (docs/research/auction_replay_v1/breadth_by_quarter.json: USDT perps listed >= 730 days, ranked by prior-month median daily quote volume, delisted symbols included)
control: the same simulator and data on the fixed 5-coin Book A universe
data: Binance daily kline archives (closes; Book A uses daily closes only), re-indexed to the simulator's end-of-day convention, forward-filled after delisting
known_simplifications: quarterly universe changes are applied at the next weekly rebalance; holdings outside the new universe are sold then
a delisted coin is valued at its last close until the next rebalance sells it
gates_stress_all_required: month-block bootstrap 95% lower bound of mean daily PnL > 0
reading: PASS = Book A's logic generalises beyond its hindsight universe -> worth strengthening and scaling. FAIL = Book A's historical result is not evidence of a durable edge.
no_parameter_search: one configuration; any change requires a new id
